projects.name: PRISM
projects.summary: Zero-trust analytics. Excel, CSV and XML are processed in your browser. No bytes leave the machine.
projects.body: A web analytics platform for sensitive information. Files are parsed and analysed in the browser with Pyodide and WebAssembly, so the data never reaches a server. AI-driven insights run on the same principle: the machine you own does the work.

projects.name: BigFish
projects.summary: An autonomous predictive terminal for sports markets. An agent swarm that watches, models and acts on its own schedule.
projects.body: BigFish is a fleet, not a script. Agents watch the market, model outcomes and act on a schedule with no human in the loop. It is the clearest public example of how Jesun builds: roles, seats and jobs, run like a company.

projects.name: PulseKey
projects.summary: Measures how a person draws. 32 metrics per session from coordinates, time and pressure. A research build, not a clinical product.
projects.body: Built during the mentAImage internship (Jan to Mar 2026). Seven drawing tasks, from clock drawing to two-hand loops. The pipeline reads tremor, pauses, speed and pressure stability, and maps 10 indicators to stress, anxiety, burnout and cognitive load scores. 35 sessions analysed. The validation study is the open work.

projects.name: NoPara
projects.summary: Private media converter. Video, audio and image conversion with FFmpeg.wasm. Zero uploads, zero tracking.
projects.body: A serverless media conversion platform. FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly runs in the browser tab, so files are converted without ever being uploaded.

projects.name: SonicClear
projects.summary: Full-stack audio cleanup. Deep learning removes background noise and restores vocal clarity.
projects.body: A full-stack web application that cleans and enhances spoken audio. A PyTorch model removes background noise; FastAPI serves it.

projects.name: TriDrop
projects.summary: Peer-to-peer file sharing between iPhone and Windows. Scan a QR code, connect, share. No install.
projects.body: WebRTC moves files directly between devices in the browser. A QR code pairs them. Nothing sits on a server in between.

projects.name: Refract
projects.summary: Privacy-focused asset generator for Chrome Web Store listings. Runs entirely in the browser.
projects.body: Store listing assets made in the browser tab, with nothing uploaded. Pinned on his GitHub profile.

projects.name: Fabric defect detection
projects.summary: Wavelet transform plus neural network to detect and classify fabric defects. AIP Conference Proceedings.
projects.body: Published research: an autonomous framework that uses the wavelet transform to expose texture defects and a neural network to classify them. Try a live version of the wavelet step in the Lab.

projects.name: Elitist PSO
projects.summary: Elitist particle swarm optimization with a mutation operator and adaptive inertia weight. AIP Conference Proceedings.
projects.body: Published research on global optimization: particle swarm optimization that keeps an elite, mutates to escape local minima and adapts inertia over time. A live version runs in the Lab.

faq.a: Jesun Ahmad Ushno is a Toronto-based software engineer who builds AI and data systems, agent fleets and machine learning products. He is the Founder of Immitly and Co-Founder of Brimwood Innovation and Climeam. He holds an MSc in Data Analytics with Distinction from the University of Niagara Falls Canada and has published two peer-reviewed machine learning papers and four sole-author preprints.

faq.q: What does Jesun Ahmad Ushno do?
faq.a: He builds production AI systems: machine learning products, retrieval-augmented generation and multi-agent fleets that run like a company, with roles, seats and jobs. He also runs three ventures: Immitly as Founder, and Brimwood Innovation and Climeam as Co-Founder.

Immitly, an immigration guidance platform, which he founded. Brimwood Innovation, a Toronto innovation hub he co-founded with Adam Sayani. Climeam, an AI-native creative studio he co-founded and whose work he directs.

Two machine learning papers in AIP Conference Proceedings (2023): one on fabric defect detection with the wavelet transform and a neural network (DOI 10.1063/5.0148618), one on an elitist particle swarm optimizer with mutation and adaptive inertia (DOI 10.1063/5.0148658). In 2026 he published four sole-author preprints on Zenodo: Peeking, Pooling, and a Locked Split (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24282470), Creditworthy Rejects (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24283751), Filtered Vector Search Is a Regime Map, Not a Leaderboard (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24283784), and Where MapReduce Catches Up (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24283816). He also wrote a book on data analytics (2025) and essays on Medium.

faq.q: Where is Jesun Ahmad Ushno based?
faq.a: Toronto, Ontario, Canada. He is from Bangladesh, where he studied computer engineering at AIUB and worked in IT Advisory at KPMG Bangladesh before moving to Canada for his MSc.
